cells.reasoning: Applicability is role-based only: HTML checkbox inputs (aria-label 'Select task'/'Select invoice') and text inputs ('Invoices count', 'Search invoice') are test targets. None has aria-invalid, :invalid, error text, role=alert or error classes in the snapshot, so each target has no form field error indicator and all three expectations hold.

The only visible text below threshold is the single glyph « in span inside div#sidebarbutton (title "Collapse sidebar"), #fff on #ccc = 1.61:1. Like the rule's Passed Example 7 (button "X"), an arrow glyph expresses nothing in human language, so it is excepted. The other ~1300 visible text nodes meet 4.5:1 (or 3:1 when large).

The three meta[name=viewport] content values are "width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" / "initial-scale=1"; none has a maximum-scale or user-scalable key, so no content attribute meets the applicability.

The only visible svg with an empty name (the 162x162 illustration in div.article-footer__svg-container) is inside section[aria-labelledby=feedback], named 'Help improve MDN'; an ancestor named from author triggers the exception. svg.logo__image has role=img and <title>MDN; the footer logo svgs have <title> names inside aria-labelled links. No img or canvas is visible.

Only fields with listed roles: input#mdbook-sidebar-toggle-anchor (checkbox, display:none) and input#mdbook-searchbar (search, under a display:none ancestor). Neither has any form field error indicator (no aria-invalid, error text or error styling on the page), so nothing can be tested; per the corpus convention a field with no error indicator does not make this rule applicable.

The role list has required owned elements (listitem). The visible sidebar ol.chapter (280px wide, in the accessibility tree) and its nested ol.section lists own only li children (no aria-owns on the page). The only menu, ul#mdbook-theme-list, is display:none so it is not a target. Every applicable list owns only listitems.

The header home link a[href='/'] in div.uwu-hidden holds a visible 40x40 React atom svg with no role, no title, empty accessible name, and no ancestor named from author (the link has no aria-label/title). The svg is the brand logo, informative rather than purely decorative; adjacent 'React' text does not change that under this rule. The unnamed search and Copy-page icon svgs are similar.

The only explicit roles with a required context are the five button[role=tab] (.sp-tab-button). Each is inside div.w-[fit-content].invisible, whose computed visibility is hidden (.invisible{visibility:hidden}), so the tabs are not included in the accessibility tree. No other element has an explicit role (listitem, option, row, cell, menuitem, treeitem...) needing a context.

svg.govuk-footer__licence-logo is visible (41x17 at 160,1595), aria-hidden=true so not in the accessibility tree, and has no named-from-author ancestor. Its path draws the Open Government Licence 'OGL' mark, which identifies the licence; that is information, not pure decoration. Adjacent licence text makes it redundant, which the rule note says still fails.

The page has no HTML img element and no HTML-namespace element with semantic role img. The only role=img element is svg.govuk-header__logotype, whose namespaceURI is http://www.w3.org/2000/svg, so it is an SVG element, not an HTML element as the applicability requires. Footer svgs are role=presentation or aria-hidden.

Four HTML radio inputs (#whereDoYouLive to #whereDoYouLive-4) have semantic role radio, so the rule applies regardless of error state. The snapshot has no aria-invalid, :invalid, govuk-error-message/summary or error styling, so each target has no form field error indicator and every expectation is satisfied.

The single meta[name=viewport] has content 'width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover', which contains neither a maximum-scale nor a user-scalable key, so no content attribute meets the applicability.

The only element with a lang attribute is html (lang=en). The rule requires the element to be an inclusive descendant of body in the flat tree; html is body's ancestor, and no element inside body carries lang, so there is no test target.

svg.govuk-footer__licence-logo is visible (41x17 at 160,725), aria-hidden=true so excluded from the accessibility tree, with no named-from-author ancestor. Its path draws the Open Government Licence 'OGL' mark identifying the licence, so it conveys information and is not purely decorative; the adjacent licence text only makes it redundant, which per the rule note still fails.

The page has no img element. The only element with role=img is svg.govuk-header__logotype, which is in the SVG namespace, not an HTML element (glossary: namespaced element), so it is outside this rule and is covered by the SVG rule instead. The footer svgs are role=presentation and aria-hidden respectively.

The only meta name=viewport has content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover", which contains neither a maximum-scale nor a user-scalable key, so no content attribute meets the applicability.

svg.govuk-footer__licence-logo is visible and aria-hidden=true, so it is excluded from the accessibility tree and applicable. It draws the Open Government Licence (OGL) logo; adjacent text makes it redundant, but per the rule note an informative icon with adjacent text is not purely decorative, so it fails. svg.govuk-footer__crown (role=presentation) is also applicable.

svg.gem-c-search__icon (aria-hidden, 20x20, visible) in the homepage button.gem-c-search__submit: the button's text "Search GOV.UK" is hidden by text-indent:-5000px, so the magnifier is the only visual label, not purely decorative; no named-from-author ancestor. svg.govuk-footer__licence-logo (OGL logo, aria-hidden, 41x17) is likewise informative (cf. Inapplicable Ex. 8).

Measured all 121 visible text nodes offline. With images/video unloaded, text over media sits on the opaque bg-carbon-black wrapper (#000) under the skrim gradient: white text is 21:1. Lowest: 'Learn More' white on rgb(216,57,51) 4.61:1 (22px bold, large, needs 3:1); '422 Images' rgb(113,113,115) on white 4.87:1 (needs 4.5:1). None below threshold.

All img elements are broken offline (naturalWidth 0) so excepted. Applicable: visible unnamed inline svg icons (graphics-document, empty name, links named from content). The svg.square-2 icons in Featured News cards use a distinct glyph per type (News Release / Article / Blog bubble) beside the matching label: informative icon marked decorative with adjacent text, which the rule's note says fails.

svg.index-module__EJ526G__icon (aria-hidden, 12x12, visible) inside the nav links "Beta Docs" and "Contribute" (target=_blank, no aria-label on any ancestor) is an external-link arrow conveying that the link opens an external site in a new tab; that information is nowhere in the text, so the image is not purely decorative.

input#signin-email (type=email, role textbox) and the Remember-me input[type=checkbox] (role checkbox) are applicable targets. With scripts off the form is novalidate and the page has no error text, aria-invalid, .is-invalid or role=alert, so each target has no form field error indicator and all three expectations hold vacuously.

The only landmark is main#content (the form is unnamed, the banner div has no role). Its first perceivable content is a.navbar-brand[aria-label=Tabler] with the visible 110x32 logo svg, a block repeated on the linked pages (., ./sign-up.html, ./forgot-password.html) that share the same logo header. Non-repeated content (h1 'Login to your account') comes only after it.

The single meta[name=viewport] has content 'width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover', which contains neither a maximum-scale nor a user-scalable key, so no content attribute meets the applicability.

The only instrument is a.skip-link href='#content', which moves focus to main#content. The first perceivable content after main is a.navbar-brand (Tabler logo link, repeated on the linked sign-up/forgot-password/index pages), so main is just before repeated content, not just before a node of non-repeated content (the h1). No other skip link or focus-moving control exists.

Applicable targets exist: input.mw-searchInput[type=search] (searchbox, visible 404x32) and the Appearance radio inputs (role radio). No element on the page has aria-invalid, an error message, or error presentation, so each target has no form field error indicator and all three expectations hold.

The six backlinks such as a#mwAss (href #cite_ref-sec1095_1-1) hide their span but carry ::before { content: counter(mw-ref-linkback, lower-alpha) } rendered as a visible letter (7px box). Accname step 2F.ii includes CSS generated textual content in name from content, so the name is non-empty. All other in-tree links have text, alt or aria-label names.

input#searchInput (search), the skin-client-pref radios and the dropdown checkboxes have listed roles, but none carries any form field error indicator: no aria-invalid, aria-errormessage, error text or error styling exists on the page. With nothing for the expectations to test, per the corpus convention the rule is inapplicable.

The page has no svg or canvas elements. Every img (including img.mw-logo-icon alt="" aria-hidden and the noscript 1x1 alt="" img) has a remote https src; with the network off the browser reports naturalWidth 0 (broken), so each img's current request is not completely available and the rule's exception removes all of them.

svg.gem-c-share-links__svg (aria-hidden, 30x30, visible) in the links "Share on Facebook" and "Share on X" are the Facebook and X logos, informative icons whose meaning is only duplicated by adjacent text, which per the rule's note and Inapplicable Example 8 is not purely decorative. svg.govuk-footer__licence-logo (OGL logo, aria-hidden) fails for the same reason.

svg.govuk-footer__licence-logo (aria-hidden, visible 41x17, no aria-label/labelledby ancestor) is the Open Government Licence logo, an informative mark only duplicated by the adjacent licence sentence, so not purely decorative. The main search icon is excepted (ancestor div#keywords[role=search][aria-label=Sitewide]), as is the pagination arrow (nav[aria-label=Pagination]).

main#content is the only candidate landmark; its first perceivable content is h4 "Business settings" plus nav[aria-label=Business settings] (links My Account, Plans -> ./settings-plan.html). Whether that sub-navigation is repeated depends on settings-plan.html, which is not in the file: if repeated, main starts with repeated content and fails; if not, it passes. The h1 sits outside any landmark.

a.skip-link "Skip to main content" href="#content" moves focus to main#content, which is just before h4 "Business settings" and the settings sub-navigation, not before the "My Account" form. Whether that sub-navigation is repeated on the linked ./settings-plan.html cannot be determined from the file, and the answer flips on it. No other in-page instrument targets later content.

No explicit roles exist, but four ul elements have the implicit list role, which has required owned elements (listitem), and all are in the accessibility tree. ul[data-testid=products-list] owns eight li, the footer Collections ul four li and the Medusa ul three li, all plain li (listitem); ul[data-testid=footer-categories] owns nothing. No list owns a non-listitem element.

Input rule 047fe0 passes: h1[data-testid=store-page-title] 'All products' is visible (955x48), in the accessibility tree, and is non-repeated content that follows the repeated header block (nav with Medusa Store / Account / Cart links, repeated on the linked /us and /us/account pages). The composite passes when any one input rule passes.

input#criteria_search_value (type=text, HTML element with semantic role textbox) is a test target; applicability does not depend on errors. It has no aria-invalid, is not :invalid, and the page has no error message, alert or error styling, so it has no form field error indicator and all expectations hold.

Implicit roles count as semantic roles. Two visible table elements (table.table.mb-3 and table.table-borderless) have role table and own only tbody (rowgroup); each tbody owns only tr (row); each tr owns only td (cell). No aria-busy ancestor, no aria-owns. Every target owns only roles from its required owned elements list.
The only meta[name=viewport] has content="width=1120", which contains neither a maximum-scale nor a user-scalable key, so no content attribute meets the applicability.

table#mwQg (implicit role table, visible, in the accessibility tree) has a direct child caption element ("List of countries and territories by total population", display table-caption) whose semantic role is caption and which is exposed as a child of the table. WAI-ARIA 1.2 lists only row and rowgroup -> row as required owned elements of table, so the table owns an element outside that list.

The ten backlinks a#mwD1I, #mwD2g, #mwELE, #mwERE, #mwFDc, #mwFDk, #mwF5k, #mwGTY, #mwGTg, #mwGeM hide their span but have ::before { content: counter(mw-ref-linkback, lower-alpha) } rendered as a visible letter; accname step 2F.ii includes CSS generated text in name from content, so the name is non-empty. Every other in-tree link has a text, alt or aria-label name.
